en.name: Dry soup mix and bouillon
en.summary: Dry soup mixes and bouillon keep 1 year from purchase in the cupboard, and 1 year after opening as well. The salt and the dryness do the preserving; what you lose over time is aroma, not safety.
en.pantry: Cool, dry and dark, 1 year from purchase and 1 year from opening — an unusual case where opening the pack barely moves the figure, because the product is essentially salt, dried vegetables, fat and flavouring with almost no free water. Humidity is still the thing to guard against: bouillon powder cakes into a brick in a steamy kitchen, and wrapped cubes go sticky and eventually mould at the foil edges. Store cubes in their wrappers inside a sealed tin, decant powder into an airtight jar, and keep both off the shelf above the kettle.
en.fridge: There is no need to refrigerate dry soup mix or bouillon, and the fridge is actively bad for it: it is a humid environment, the pack is opened and closed repeatedly, and a salty powder is hygroscopic enough to draw moisture out of the air and set solid. The cupboard, sealed and dry, is where it belongs. Made-up stock is a different food — it is a wet, low-acid liquid, so cool it quickly, refrigerate it at 4 °C (40 °F) or below, and treat it as you would any cooked broth.
en.freezer: No freezer timeline is published for dry soup mix or bouillon, and a sealed jar that keeps a year in a cupboard has nothing to gain from the freezer except condensation on the way out. Made-up stock, on the other hand, freezes very well — reduce it, freeze it in an ice cube tray, and you have concentrated stock on demand. That is the useful application of the freezer here, not the dry product.
spoilage: Powder caked into a solid block that will not break up.
A stale or rancid smell from the fat in the mix.
Sticky, weeping cubes, or mould at the edges of the foil wrapper.
Insects, moths or webbing in the box or jar.
tips: Decant powder into an airtight jar; cardboard cartons let damp in.
Keep the tin away from the kettle and the hob.
Write the opening date on the jar — flavour fades before anything else happens.
Freeze made-up stock in ice cube trays rather than keeping it in the fridge for days.

faq.q: How long do stock cubes and bouillon powder keep?
faq.a: 1 year from purchase, and 1 year after opening, kept dry and sealed in a cool cupboard.
No. The fridge is humid and a salty powder will cake solid. Keep it sealed in a dry cupboard.

faq.q: Is caked bouillon powder still usable?
faq.a: It is usually safe if it smells clean, but it has taken up moisture and the flavour will have faded. Break it up and check for any musty smell or mould.

zh.name: 乾燥湯粉與高湯塊
zh.summary: 乾燥湯粉與高湯塊從購買日起算放櫥櫃 1 年，開封之後也是 1 年。保存靠的是鹽與乾燥；隨時間流失的是香氣，不是安全性。
zh.pantry: 陰涼、乾燥、避光，自購買日起 1 年，開封後同樣 1 年——這是少見的「開封幾乎不改變數字」的情況，因為它基本上就是鹽、乾燥蔬菜、油脂與調味料，幾乎沒有自由水。但要防的仍然是濕氣：在蒸氣瀰漫的廚房裡，高湯粉會結成一塊磚，鋁箔包的湯塊會變黏，最後從包裝邊緣長霉。湯塊連著包裝放進密封鐵盒，粉類倒進氣密罐，兩者都不要放在熱水壺上方的層架。
zh.fridge: 乾燥湯粉與高湯塊不需要冷藏，冰箱對它反而有害：那是個潮濕的環境，包裝又會被反覆開關，而含鹽的粉末吸濕性很強，會從空氣中把水抓過來、然後凝成硬塊。密封、乾燥的櫥櫃才是它的位置。泡好的高湯則是另一種食物：那是含水的低酸性液體，要快速降溫、放 4 °C 以下冷藏，並且比照任何煮好的高湯來管理。
zh.freezer: 乾燥湯粉與高湯塊沒有公布的冷凍期限，而一罐密封後能在櫥櫃放一年的東西，從冷凍得到的只有拿出來時的結露。反過來說，泡好的高湯非常適合冷凍——煮濃一點，倒進製冰盒，隨時有濃縮高湯可用。冷凍庫在這裡該發揮的是這個用途，而不是拿來冰乾貨。
spoilage: 粉體結成敲不散的硬塊。
配方裡的油脂發出陳味或油耗味。
湯塊發黏出水，或鋁箔邊緣長霉。
盒子或罐子裡有蟲、蛾或絲網。
tips: 粉類倒進氣密罐，紙盒擋不住濕氣。
鐵盒遠離熱水壺與爐台。
在罐上寫開封日期，香氣會比其他變化更早消失。
泡好的高湯用製冰盒冷凍，不要在冷藏放好幾天。

faq.a: 保持乾燥密封放陰涼櫥櫃，自購買日起 1 年，開封後也是 1 年。
不需要。冰箱潮濕，含鹽的粉會凝成硬塊。請密封放乾燥的櫥櫃。

faq.q: 結塊的高湯粉還能用嗎？
faq.a: 只要聞起來乾淨，通常還能用，但它已經吸了水氣、香氣也變淡了。敲散之後確認沒有霉味或霉點。
